escalations.residual_risk: max_paths is a live guard, not dead weight. After removal the remaining dimensions are max_depth, max_listings, max_bytes. Listing-driven expansion stays bounded because RepositoryImage::close folds every listing child's name length into byte_count (image.rs:777-779, 832-833). Caller-enqueued fixed/discovered/pinned/linked_worktree paths are the dimension that may become unbounded: a zero-byte entry contributes nothing to byte_count. The worker was instructed to state the bounding argument per path source, to close any gap through a dimension derived from what the model constrains rather than a renamed path count, and to stop and report as blocking if the removal cannot be made safe. This is a trust boundary: capture reads manifest-declared targets, and under `jit profile add` the manifest arrives from outside the repository.

escalations.question: Does the edit-and-refresh loop have to cover every profile-owned content class in v1.0?
escalations.evidence: Verified all four classes against a built binary. Live-source asset: capture+apply refreshes, validate clean. Install-only asset: capture no-op, apply conflicts. Managed region: capture no-op, apply silently discards the edit. Semantic contribution: capture no-op, apply and reconfigure both report 'unchanged', jit validate fails permanently with a profile-ownership rule error and --fix offers nothing.
escalations.owner_decision: Cover all classes, but the owner challenged reading region bodies back since that content is generated. Region clobber ruled intended: regions are profile-owned territory the package re-renders.
escalations.lead_resolution: The owner's principle generalizes: refresh applies where the REPOSITORY authors the content. Live-source assets (already works) and semantic contributions (5a3ecba0) qualify. Regions and install-only assets are package-authored - a region body is generated from the region source, and install-only content is adopter state the authoring repository holds in a different form, guarded by test_live_assets_exclude_install_only_adopter_state. Neither has a repository-side value to read back.
escalations.lead_correction: The lead's own option text claimed that if the region clobber is intended then profile validate should stop reporting it, 'since nothing acts on that report'. That was wrong: jit profile apply re-renders the region and validate goes green, so the report is actionable and needs no change.

surfaced_pitfalls.subject: live-asset classification encoded twice
surfaced_pitfalls.detail: Whether a package asset draws its bytes from the repository is answered by a package-relative source path prefix (JIT_DOGFOOD_LIVE_SOURCE_PREFIX = "assets/live/", crates/jit/src/profile/repository_package.rs:5, consumed in production only at package_assembly.rs:190) while the manifest separately declares [[live-source]] roots (manifest.rs:149, LiveSourceDeclaration at :346). Two encodings of one convention (@/inv/convention-convergence), and the constant names one package for a rule applied to every package (@/inv/domain-agnostic). The epic plan fixes the prefix convention for REQ-13, so 6a479c58 is directed to rename the constant only; converging on a declared per-asset marker would be a manifest-schema change beyond the plan.
surfaced_pitfalls.reconciliation_2026_08_13: Half fixed, half live. The domain-agnostic half is closed: the constant no longer names one package (JIT_DOGFOOD_LIVE_SOURCE_PREFIX renamed to LIVE_ASSET_SOURCE_PREFIX, manifest.rs:20), so no site names a particular package for a rule applied to every package. The convention-convergence half is live and load-bearing in production: whether an asset draws its bytes from the repository is decided BOTH by a hardcoded path prefix (package_capture.rs:187 'authority: if asset.source.starts_with(LIVE_ASSET_SOURCE_PREFIX)', repository_package.rs:334 and :347 filtering on the same prefix) AND by the manifest's declared [[live-source]] roots (manifest.rs:159, LiveSourceDeclaration at :357). Two encodings of one convention, both live. Bears on epic REQ-12 ('no adapter, dual format, fallback behavior, temporary compatibility code, or duplicated workflow inventory') and on @/inv/convention-convergence. Per lead-review-protocol, the plan deferring it binds the fan-out shape only and cannot make an unmet criterion met: this needs either a remediation task inside the container or positive evidence it is not a REQ-12 violation, BEFORE the f6a17e0d/dd268d0f checkpoints and the epic gate.
surfaced_pitfalls.resolution: Owner accepted the lead's finding, 2026-08-13. The 'encoded twice' framing was wrong. PRODUCTION HAS ONE CLASSIFIER: crates/jit/src/profile/package_capture.rs:187, inside declared_sources, keying on the assets/live/ prefix; capture_package_tree reads only declared_sources(&model) and consults live_sources nowhere. The two other sites handoff-11 cited, repository_package.rs:334 and :347, are inside #[cfg(test)] mod tests - that module opens at repository_package.rs:3 - so they are this repository's own dogfood conformance suite, not a production decision. Every PRODUCTION read of model.live_sources is package.rs:761-788 (validate_live_source_roots, non-overlap only), variables.rs:575 (rejecting variable references in roots and exclusions), and wire.rs:97/:153 (pass-through). None classifies an asset. The two mechanisms answer different questions: the prefix decides which side owns a declared asset's bytes; the declared roots bound a completeness walk over repository directories that must be fully packaged. REQ-12 forbids an adapter, dual format, fallback, temporary compatibility code, or duplicated workflow inventory; none is present, because there is no second decision path to remove.
surfaced_pitfalls.residual: One real but separate observation, not a REQ-12 violation: nothing in the package model requires a live asset's target to fall under a declared [[live-source]] root. That correspondence is asserted only by test_declared_live_source_roots_claim_every_live_asset_target_exactly_once, a dogfood conformance test over this repository's own package. An adopter manifest could declare a live asset outside every declared root and nothing would reject it. Recorded rather than assumed.
surfaced_pitfalls.caveat: Rests on the lead's own trace. The independent cross-check dispatched for it hung on stdin - the known codex-exec-blocks-on-stdin pitfall - and was killed after four hours without producing output.

measurements.finding: Idle-host suite baseline, for judging any test this epic adds against the enforced 30 s budget.
measurements.detail: Three warm runs on a quiet host at 0e71077d9, measured by the peer session holding both locks: suite-clock 22175 / 23628 / 22095 ms, total gate 24821 / 26307 / 24794 ms, suite-build 356-377 ms, 4481 tests, 7 skipped, 63 doctests, every run exit 0. Recorded as 4ced8862b under dev/benchmarks/suite-enforcement-4b7c06d0/ with the contended run beside it. Under one concurrent cold workspace build the same tree measured 29477 ms and passed by 523 ms, with incremental-state (a directory walk) going 130 ms to 11497 ms and doctests 4600 to 7706 ms on pure I/O contention. Roughly 7 s of headroom on an idle host; roughly 0.5 s under one concurrent build.
measurements.standing_rule: Consecutive gate runs are not independent samples: the middle of those three is the high one because it started while the previous run's load was still decaying. A back-to-back reading that looks bad is the previous run, not the change under test. Let the host settle between measurements. Corollary for this epic: cf42d08b's regression test publishes 511 assets at nine path components through the real transaction and must be timed in isolation before merge.

measurements.finding: The first gate run in a worktree that just absorbed a large merge is not a measurement of the change. It reads roughly 15 s high on this host and fails the 30 s suite budget.
measurements.detail: Reproduced independently on both wave-13/14 worktrees. cf42d08b cold: suite-clock 37761 ms, FAILED; warm: 22218 ms, passed twice. f2389b18 cold: FAILED; warm: 22128 ms, passed. The discriminator is the suite-build step, which measured 36966 ms cold against 353 ms warm — it keeps compilation outside the measured clock by design, but cannot pre-warm the page cache for artifacts written seconds earlier, so the test step pays first-touch I/O inside the clock (33274 ms cold vs 17570 ms warm on the same shared 4481-test core). A failure of this shape names a cold worktree, not the change and not the budget.
measurements.standing_rule: Gate a freshly merged worktree twice, letting the host settle between runs, and read only the second. Never diagnose a suite-duration failure without first checking uptime and whether anything else was compiling.

measurements.finding: Suite wall-clock is a critical path, not a sum. Adding test time does not add it to the suite.
measurements.detail: cf42d08b's three new tests measure 4.56 s in isolation (the 511-asset regression test alone is 4.55 s, just under the suite's 5324 ms slowest existing test); f2389b18's seven measure 0.643 s. Predicted suite impact by addition: ~5.2 s onto a 22095 ms baseline. Measured impact: 22218 ms and 22128 ms — roughly 0.1 s. nextest runs process-per-test across 24 workers, so an expensive test lengthens wall-clock only if it lands last on the critical path. The additive model would have imposed a false constraint on every remaining wave of this epic and led to shrinking tests to buy margin that was never being consumed.
measurements.standing_rule: Measure a test's suite impact by running the suite, not by adding the test's isolated cost to a baseline. Isolated cost answers 'is this test expensive', which is a different question from 'does this test cost the suite anything'.

measurements.verdict: KEEP the gate-run ban. The 19 GiB figure is obsolete, but the conclusion it supported survives re-measurement: one --all-targets build costs 1.8 GiB of incremental state on the CURRENT 10-target topology, and a gate run compiles once and exits, so that 1.8 GiB buys nothing unless the same tree is gated again against a small delta. At 14 worktrees and 86% disk, gating every tree once with incremental on is roughly 25 GiB against 128 GiB free.
measurements.counterweight_recorded_not_acted_on: Incremental WOULD pay for the one access pattern this workflow has plenty of: re-gating one worker worktree across rework rounds. 96268a98 was gated twice, each round paying ~37 s suite-build and ~27 s clippy from scratch. If disk pressure eases, the case to revisit is per-worktree incremental for rework rounds specifically, not a blanket lift.
measurements.caveat: Wall-clock was NOT measured: the host was compiling for 0708d692 throughout (load 4.6 rising to 10.8), and the archived protocol itself requires an isolated repeated protocol rather than timings taken under load. Disk is load-independent, which is why the disk half was taken now. Any decision resting on the wall-clock half still needs a quiet host.
measurements.cleanup: The 1.8 GiB of incremental state produced by this measurement was removed; that worktree's target went 9.0 -> 7.3 GiB. It remains above its 5.3 GiB pre-measurement size because the CARGO_INCREMENTAL=1 fingerprint rebuilt artifacts alongside the originals.
